score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

assessment.rationale: Good fit for the durable audit-publication half of the scenario, weak fit for live CRDT transport itself. The design keeps the universal envelope minimal and confines richer subject/assertion/proof structure to a payload-family pCID, which cleanly separates audit-layer interpretation from generic transport. That helps later review and evolution, but the specimen does not define the exact save-time audit object, live-channel recovery semantics, or promise-first wording.
strengths: Very clear layer boundary: universal outer envelope stays tiny while richer audit structure is payload-local.
Deterministic CBOR arrays and unknown-pCID rules support durable preservation and partial interpretation.
Subject/assertion/proof wrapper can improve later audit and attribution without forcing all peers to adopt it.
Good evolution posture because Gordian-style structure is optional and pCID-scoped rather than universal.
weaknesses: Does not specify a live reliable ordered channel or reconnection behavior for the CRDT path.
Leaves unclear what exact content-addressed snapshot object the save-time audit message should cite.
Uses Gordian assertion/proof vocabulary more than promise-first payload promises.
Adds wrapper complexity compared with a smaller audit artifact.
risks: Audit wrapper semantics could drift toward generic claim-card framing instead of explicit peer promises.
Implementers may overread the specimen as a live protocol shape rather than an audit publication format.
Extra structure may be too heavy for small-device simplicity if adopted too broadly.
open_questions: Should live CRDT traffic stay off-grid entirely until a reliable binding exists?
What precise snapshot/state object should the audit message reference at save time?
How should a human-readable promise body map onto subject/assertion/proof fields without losing promise-first clarity?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
